A fun game that lets you do "Hollywood hacking", with all the pretty eye-catching graphics that come with it.  You receive a mission via email, you do the thing, you get the next mission, repeat.  At some points you get to choose from a selection of missions.

It's casual and fun.  Hacking of a computer follows a pretty basic pattern that simply adds on more steps as the game goes on, but it's still fun -- even if the hacking is very similar, each mission has enough depth and background going on that you want to move on to do the next one, and the Hollywood hacking makes you feel the part.  When the active traces start showing up later in the game, it's a real adrenaline surge.  At some point in the game you'll compromise a computer requiring eight different steps and just feel a sense of achievement about the whole thing.

(Note that this is not real hacking any more than playing a FPS is real combat.  The game requires no technical knowledge, and will give you only the barest of real-world-usable knowledge in return.  It is entertainment, not instructive.)

Excellent game. Can't really say about how accurate/realistic it is, but it's definitely really enjoyable and immersive. There's a lot of nice easter eggs and secrets scattered throughout, that are pretty fun to explore.

I love quest-style campaigns in general, especially ones that feel pretty organic. There wasn't a whole lot of replay value though, outside of a good 2-3 runs to go through everything, by the end of which the mechanics started feeling a little stale and linear. But dang that first run when you're just bombarded with new things feels amazing—the learning curve in the game is fantastic, giving you nudges but forcing you to figure out a lot on your own.

Some stuff was kinda iffy, especially the janky file manipulation commands (needing to use append and replace only?), the rather picky requirements to unlock a certain achievement, and the cluttered mess that was the netMap, but by and large it felt pretty good and polished the whole way through.

And always remember: don't forget to clear your logs!

Hacknet is quite an amazing game. It may not look or sound like much, but I guarantee that you'll be hooked shortly after you start playing. It has an amazing story as well as a great soundtrack that really fits the game. Additionally, it isn't too resource-demanding, so even if you have a potato for a PC, you can probably still play it!
If you're looking for more after finishing the main game, you can get the Labyrinths DLC, and the Hacknet community has published many Extensions (essentially custom stories) to the Workshop.
I recommend Hacknet to anyone who wants a unique experience, but also a fun one.

Hacknet is a really cool hacking simulator where you play as a hacker using a UNIX-based hacking operating system called HacknetOS. You are contacted by a fellow hacker, and go on a wild ride of hacking and dealing with other hackers and hacking organizations. The game may not be realisticly EXACTLY what hacking is like, but it's not one of those games where you do puzzles to hack people like I origionally thought it'd be. You actually have to learn BASH terminal commands to navigate a file system and call commands to run programs and stuff like that. You can mostly use the graphical interface to navigate, but at some point, you're forced to use only commands, so it's important to learn them. It's easy if you're a fast typer and are already familiar with UNIX operating systems (like Linux). If you're not, it's still pretty fun to learn and play, even if it's not the real thing. I couldn't help thinking, "If only I could do this in real life," while playing this game.

Hacknet is a puzzle game that revolves around the usage of several executable files to progress the story.  The storyline itself was incredible, and I personally loved the game's mechanics as well.  It may be challenging at times, but it isn't too challenging.  There are always programs to make the game easier as well, and the community is incredible to be a part of.  The soundtrack was very fitting for the game, with a cyberpunk vibe for most puzzle based parts,  and emotional music for the end of the story.

This game will test your logistic skills and typing speed at every turn. Thematically, it really does feel like you're a hacker from the movies, and the story unravels through psudonymous contacts and automated emails from Bit. The soundtrack is 100%, and the panic when you get a trace alert is real and shocking every time. The game is absolutely studded with easter eggs, bits of lore, and plenty of cyberspace to explore. The Labyrinths DLC adds a few extra missions with two different endings which are not connected to the main story, but can give you a quick boost if you do them first, but you can just as well do them afterward. After completing the story, there is a sort of "free roam" mode where you can do everything you never got the chance to do during the main missions.

I got hacknet under the guise of being a cute game about cartoonish movie hacking but was left much more impressed and engaged at the end than I ever thought I would be. The game has a fantastic soundtrack to keep the flow going and the hacker missions you're given (and sign up for) get progressively more interesting from a puzzle solving perspective. There's great elements of sheer terror that crop up, where I had to dig through my filesystem to find a piece of code to run before time ran out. There's some genuinely great surprises in this game and the text-based nature of it works very well for what it is. In the final third of the game, I felt like a hacker you see in the movies. Hacknet really keeps getting better the more you play it and is perfectly paced and just the right length. Such a gem!

Great game. It is very immersive and challenging. Figuring out and having that aha moment is nice treat that most games don't have. The soundtrack is really good, I find myself playing it all the time. There were a lot of secrets, and the game really rewarded you for being thorugh.

I love hacknet for riding the fine line between some realism and interesting fantasy perfect. Chatrooms and characters feel great and while some are stereotypical, that's legitimately how some people are in forums. The most important part of the game, sifting through networks of computers to solve the various missions feel smooth and comprehensive, with plenty of difficulty on some of the missions if you don't quite find the right details. Scenarios are well spread out from goofy to serious and cover a wide range of controversial and thought provoking topics that are really good to show both sides of hacking, from kiddy groups to screwing around in forums to big groups and even small vigilante groups. I'd like to have seen more of the big business sign, possibly even in labyrinths to actually secure more systems or get more advanced, such as allowing us to create our own scripts, without punishing new players, but it's completely understandable why that wasn't done.

Great overview of programming and the idea of hacking, with plenty of fantasy to keep it interesting and uncomplicated for the average person.

This game is presented as "immersive, terminal-based hacking simulator".

I nabbed this game when it was free for 48 hours, and it sat around in my library since then, just another game in the collection. I'd been playing some co-op games lately, and, not able to progress whenever my friends were offline, I looked for a single player game to pass the time. Ultimately, I ended up selecting Hacknet. I had zero expectations for the game as I actually had no knowledge of the game itself or its gameplay. Boy, was I pleasantly surprised! I was drawn in by the unique method of storytelling and the puzzles (not to mention the fact that the game was making me feel like some sort of experienced hacker)!

If you too grabbed the game and have left it unplayed and forgotten, I recommend you give this game a chance! As of now, I'm still progressing through the game, meticulously completing every contract and poking through every file folder. In a way, perhaps I'm just taking my time as I'm reluctant for the game to end... But believe me, playing in full screen, contemplating your decisions, and roleplaying will just make your entire game experience more memorable!

You've done it. You went and got yourself a fast PC with a fast ethernet connection and now you're breaking into the hidden digital domains that were once exclusively for the hacker elite. 

Flashy interface, exicting music, sexy people, drugs...all the glamor is now yours.

PFFT....

Real hacking is boring. It involves patience, looking at countless lines of code to find valuable snippets of information. If this sounds like something you're interested in but don't want to worry about being caught, Hacknet is for you. It's a hacking simulator where your successes advance the game and your failures don't land you time in prison.
